props.name: commitBehavior
props.description: What an open range does when focus leaves the calendar or the user presses outside its days and month buttons: `"select"` completes it at the focused or hovered day, `"reset"` drops the anchor and keeps the previous range.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The range selected first, when the calendar owns its value. Takes what `value` takes.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether nothing in the calendar responds: no day takes focus and the month buttons are disabled.

props.name: firstDayOfWeek
props.description: The weekday each row starts on. Defaults to the locale's: Sunday in en-US, Monday in the Nordic locales.

props.name: isDateUnavailable
props.type: ((date: PlainDate, anchor: PlainDate | null) => boolean) | undefined
props.description: Days the user may focus but not select, given the anchored day while a range is being chosen (`null` otherwise), so the available days can depend on the first day picked. Once a range is anchored it can reach only the run of available days around the anchor, looked for up to `visibleMonths` months each way: the days past the nearest unavailable day are disabled until the range completes. An unavailable day further from the anchor is not looked for, as in React Aria, so a longer range can span it; check such a range in `onValueChange`. Keep the function's identity stable across renders, since every day re-renders when it changes.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: The last selectable day, taking what `minValue` takes. Days after it are disabled.

props.name: minValue
props.description: The first selectable day: a Temporal PlainDate, PlainDateTime or ZonedDateTime from any implementation. A date-time bound counts from its own wall-clock day. Days before it are disabled, never focusable, and focus clamps to it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the user completes a range, with this runtime's `Temporal.PlainDate`s, earlier day first. The first day pressed only anchors the range and calls nothing. `details.reason` is `"day-press"`, `"keyboard"`, `"outside-press"` or `"focus-out"`. Canceling a day press or key with `details.cancel()` keeps the value and the anchor, so the user can pick another end; canceling an outside press or focus-out keeps the value and drops the anchor. `details.getValidationError()` returns `null` for a range the calendar accepts, and otherwise `"rangeUnderflow"` for a start before `minValue`, `"rangeOverflow"` for an end after `maxValue` and `"unavailable"` for an end `isDateUnavailable` refuses with no anchor.

props.name: onVisibleRangeChange
props.description: Called when the visible months change by a month button or the keyboard, with the new first month. `details.reason` is `"increment-press"`, `"decrement-press"` or `"keyboard"`. Canceling with `details.cancel()` keeps the months shown: a month button press does nothing, and a key that would page leaves focus on the day it was on.

props.name: pageBehavior
props.description: How the month buttons page a multi-month view, and how far the view moves when the keyboard leaves it: `"visible"` by every visible month, `"single"` by one.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user may move around the months but not change the value.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected range, when the parent owns it: each end a `Temporal.PlainDate` from any implementation. A range given in reverse shows the earlier day first. A server component cannot pass one, since it reaches the client as text: build the value in a client component. `null` selects nothing.

props.name: visibleMonths
props.description: How many months show side by side, wrapping onto new rows when the host is narrow. Pick it from the viewport in the host, such as one month on a phone and two on a desktop. A whole number from 1: a fraction truncates, and anything below 1 or not a finite number shows one month, with a warning in development.

props.name: aria-label

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: isPending
props.description: The in-flight state of an async action. Stamps `data-pending` and `aria-busy`, blocks activation (effective disabled is `disabled || isPending`) and renders the disabled treatment, but keeps the button in the focus order like `focusableWhenDisabled`, so a keyboard user who activated it is still on it when the result arrives. Shows the `pendingIndicator` in the leading icon position meanwhile. An explicit `focusableWhenDisabled={false}` restores the native `disabled` attribute while pending. `aria-busy` announces nothing by itself: say what is happening through the label ("Saving") or a `role="status"` region outside the button. Put a label that changes with the state in its own element, such as `{label}`: page translation replaces a bare text child with its own nodes, so React's update to the old text node never shows.

props.name: isVisuallyDisabled
props.description: Stamps `aria-disabled` (an explicit consumer value wins), which renders the disabled treatment (`opacity-50`, the `not-allowed` cursor, no hover or press paint), and suppresses focus-on-press while the button stays fully interactive — click, keyboard and focus-visible all still work, and a Tooltip on it still opens. For "looks disabled but explains itself on activation" flows. The treatment keys off `aria-disabled`, so an explicit `aria-disabled={false}` also turns it off: the button then looks and announces enabled and only the focus-on-press suppression remains.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: onIntent
props.description: Predictive-prefetch callback. Fires once when the pointer's predicted trajectory lands inside the inflated hit rect; browsers without the prediction API fail soft.

props.name: pendingIndicator
props.description: What the button shows while pending. Omitted: a spinning `SpinnerGap` in the leading icon position, and the button's own leading and bare SVG children hide so the spinner takes their place (a trailing `data-icon="inline-end"` icon stays). A node: rendered in that same place instead of the spinner, as a decorative `aria-hidden` slot; animate it yourself. `null` or `false`: no indicator and nothing hidden, so the call site owns the pending markup, for example a brand button that keeps its logo and centres its own spinner over it.

props.name: predictionZoneSize
props.description: Pixels the hit rect is inflated on every side when predicting pointer intent.
